notes: Agiorgitiko, native to Nemea, makes soft, fruity reds in many styles.
Xinomavro has great aging potential, with notes of tomato and olive and rich tannin.
Samos and Patras are known for sweet Muscat.
Nemea reds are made from Agiorgitiko, dry or sweet.
The best come from mid-slope vineyards, since the hilltops can be too acidic and the valley floor too jammy.
Santorini Assyrtiko is bone dry and full bodied, with high acidity, citrus, stone fruit and a distinct minerality.
Low-yielding vines in volcanic ash give concentrated wines with briny salinity and razor-sharp acidity.
Vinsanto, from sun-dried grapes, is golden orange to amber, with dried apricot, golden raisin, sweet spice and minerality.
Classic Naoussa has high acidity, medium color and savory aromas of tomato paste and olive.
Its tannins are firm and often aggressive, and need years of aging to soften.
Some sites give deeper color, softer tannins and riper, warmer fruit.
Aromas also take in red fruit, spice, dried plum, tobacco and nuts, and a complex bouquet forms with age.
Off-dry and medium-sweet versions are also made.
